summary: A C# Windows Forms application demonstrating core OOP principles through a simulated space fleet management system. It models spacecraft hierarchies, manages operational states, and provides an interactive UI for dynamic ship creation and mission execution.
key_features: Dynamic ship creation at runtime via modular input controls
Polymorphic mission execution with type-specific behavior
Real-time status tracking (fuel, IDs, specialized attributes)
Robust input validation and exception handling
Modular UI architecture using swappable UserControl panels
Custom indexers for cargo log management
Sealed classes to prevent unintended inheritance
achievements: Architected a multi-level OOP class hierarchy implementing abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation. Engineered a modular WinForms UI with dynamic UserControl swapping and real-time fleet state synchronization. Solved complex runtime dispatch challenges using virtual/override methods and custom indexers for cargo management. Proactively identified architectural bottlenecks (UI/logic coupling, inefficient state updates) and documented scalable solutions including Factory pattern adoption, INotifyPropertyChanged for data binding, and .resx localization.
